request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Medical History:
The patient is a 20-year-old previously healthy male who presented to the emergency department with fever and rash six days after being diagnosed with a viral upper respiratory infection at an urgent care center.

Hospital Course:
The patient was diagnosed with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) for supportive care. He required escalating amounts of supplemental oxygen during his ED course and remained hospitalized for 6 days.

Clinical Findings:
The patient presented with a diffuse, morbilliform rash across the trunk and extremities, sparing the face. A chest radiograph showed bilateral infiltrates consistent with multifocal pneumonia. Labs revealed a normal leukocyte count with an elevated C-reactive protein.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient received supportive care in the ICU, including supplemental oxygen and monitoring of vital signs.

Follow-up:
The patient is stable on hospital day 6 and will require additional monitoring and follow-up to determine the appropriate plan for discharge from the hospital.

Recommendations:
The patient should continue to follow up with his healthcare provider and monitor his symptoms closely to determine when he can safely return to his daily activities. Additionally, he should follow all recommendations and guidelines from public health officials regarding social distancing and hand hygiene to slow the spread of the virus.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: J12**

The episode is SARS-CoV-2 infection with viral pneumonia, which required ICU-level oxygen support. Viral pneumonia (J12) is the condition that best fits the chief reason for admission. In the current ICD-10-AM code set, COVID-19 is coded in the special-purpose U07.1 block, which is not among the chapters you listed, so J12 is the closest match within the given structure.
